Category_A_Codec_Mismatch.evidence: In tokenizer/codec.py lines 80-87, AudioCodecTokenizer.decode zero-padded tokens from 4 codebooks to 32 codebooks (pad_q = torch.zeros(1, 28, seq_len)). In Encodec 24 kHz, codebook index 0 in layers 4..31 is an active vector centroid. Summing 28 zero-indexed codebook vectors across all frames injected a constant, stationary 75 Hz harmonic buzzing drone (diff amplitude = 1.0315) over every reconstructed and generated audio file. When decoded purely with 4 codebooks, this drone is completely eliminated.

Category_B_Prompt_Assembly_Bug.evidence: Prompt audio extracted pre-inference and post-assembly matches bit-for-bit (max diff = 0.00000000). The assembly pipeline does not alter or corrupt the prompt waveform.

Category_C_Incorrect_Codebook_Prediction.evidence: Predicted tokens are valid integers strictly within [0, 1023]. No special tokens (1024..1027) are present in generated output. Causal masking and teacher-forced sequential depth heads function as mathematically intended.

Category_D_Model_Acoustic_Capacity.verdict: CONFIRMED PRIMARY CAUSE FOR FREE-RUNNING GENERATION
Category_D_Model_Acoustic_Capacity.evidence: In Phase 4, teacher-forced decoding (conditioned on ground-truth preceding frames at every step) achieves 5.78% top-1 accuracy on CB0 and retains formant energy, but still has an overall accuracy of 4.41% and loss of 5.68 nats (perplexity = 295 out of 1024). At 3,000 steps with single-sequence batch size on a 100-hour diverse corpus, the model has observed only ~3,000 speech segments (~1.5 hours of audio exposure out of 100 hours). The model has learned broad vowel formants (F1 ~700 Hz, F2 ~1500 Hz) and syllabic cadence, but has not yet learned high-frequency phonetic transitions or sharp consonantal boundaries.

Category_E_Autoregressive_Exposure_Bias.evidence: During training, every single step is conditioned on 100% ground-truth clean past tokens. During generation, after 20-30 autoregressively sampled frames, slight prediction errors in codebooks 0-3 feed back into the causal self-attention window. Because RVQ codes are highly sensitive to compounding drift, the attention representation drifts away from the speech manifold into a stationary limit cycle (repeating high-probability vocalic codes at ~45% repetition), which sounds like vocalic humming.

Category_F_Generation_Sampling.evidence: At temperature T=0.8 and top-k=50 with repetition penalty 1.15, the multinomial sampler over a high-entropy distribution (entropy ~5.6 nats out of log(1024)=6.93 nats) frequently samples low-probability residual codes in CB2 and CB3, producing acoustic roughness and blurring phonetic intelligibility.
